extracted.intended_audience: organizations and individuals applying for CDC grant funding; grant writers and program staff preparing NOFO applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing how CDC grant applications are reviewed and the criteria used to evaluate them, including standard evaluation categories, reviewer procedures, strategic priorities, and funding decision factors. Useful for applicants preparing proposals and for reviewers conducting merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and objective merit review
rubrics_metrics.description: The CDC ensures grant applications undergo an independent and objective merit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review process expectations include thorough and consistent examination of applications, unbiased evaluation of scientific or technical merit or other relevant aspects, reviews conducted as soon as possible after the submission deadline, and that review results are advisory to the approving program official who considers them when making final award recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation per NOFO-published criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed in accordance with evaluation criteria published in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers score applications against the published evaluation criteria for that NOFO; each NOFO has its own specific criteria which govern scoring and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary statement of strengths and weaknesses is prepared for each scored application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement documents reviewer findings and supports the numeric score; it is part of the feedback provided to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the soundness of the public health intervention and the quality of proposed methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include whether the approach is evidence-based, the clarity and appropriateness of the implementation strategy, and the quality of the data collection plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population Served
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how the application characterizes and addresses the target population's needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider population characterization, demonstrated need within the target population, strategies to ensure access, and cultural appropriateness of proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and Evaluation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and appropriateness of the proposed evaluation to measure process and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes review of process measures, outcome measures, long-term impact metrics, and the overall evaluation methodology and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant organization's ability to successfully implement the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider organizational capability, personnel qualifications, available infrastructure, and past performance on similar projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget reasonableness and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed budget for cost reasonableness and appropriate allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine whether costs are reasonable for the work proposed, properly allocated, and adequately justified in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans and likelihood for sustaining program activities after the period of CDC support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes assessment of plans for sustaining the work, diversification of resources, and built-in revenue or other support mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review format options
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit reviews for discretionary grant programs may be conducted in multiple formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format variations include face-to-face meetings, technology-enabled remote discussions, or independent assessment by individual reviewers without panel discussion; NOFO or program guidance may specify the review format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility and conflict-of-interest attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only appointed reviewers may score applications and must attest to absence of conflict of interest before reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are chosen for relevant expertise; both government and non-government reviewers may be used. Reviewers must complete COI statements to ensure unbiased evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness, equity, objectivity, and transparency of process
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit reviews are designed to ensure applications are evaluated fairly, equitably, objectively, and transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles guide reviewer selection, scoring, documentation (e.g., summary statements), and communication with applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant feedback on strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants receive feedback documenting the strengths and weaknesses identified during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback is provided via summary statements and is intended to help applicants understand review outcomes and improve future submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decisions consider scores plus programmatic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Final funding recommendations consider merit review scores in combination with programmatic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officials weigh review results alongside strategic priorities, available funds, and other programmatic considerations when making award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CDC strategic public health priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: CDC strategic priorities influence funding decisions and include specific public health focus areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed priorities include infectious disease prevention, chronic disease prevention, injury prevention, environmental health, workplace safety, maternal and child health, emergency preparedness, and health equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cutting considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-cutting factors that inform evaluation and funding decisions across programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include population health equity, stakeholder engagement, community partnerships, workforce development, and data modernization; these may be emphasized in NOFOs and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant mechanisms and award types
rubrics_metrics.description: CDC uses multiple grant and cooperative agreement mechanisms with differing expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include R01 (Research Project Grant), R18 (Research Demonstration), U01/U18/U48/U54 (Cooperative Agreements), T01-T03 (Training), cooperative agreements for state/local health departments and for community-based organizations; mechanism influences review expectations (e.g., implementation emphasis for cooperative agreements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis differences from NIH (implementation-focused review)
rubrics_metrics.description: CDC reviews often emphasize implementation, partnerships, and evaluation/dissemination over discovery research alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct features include direct partnerships with state/local health departments, the paramount importance of stakeholder engagement, and heavier weighting of evaluation and dissemination plans compared to typical NIH discovery emphasis.
